terms.comment: One of the card’s useful spatial words for building.
evidence: Traupman 204, 319: in front of, ante + accusative

terms.gloss: in front of, before (a building, a camp, a gate)
evidence: Cic. Phil. 3.27: sedēns prō aede Castoris (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 4.32: prō portīs castrōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Right in front of a thing and facing out from it, like men posted before a gate; ante with the accusative is the everyday word (Traupman 319).

sources: Lewis & Short: ante · Lewis & Short: pro
Dickinson: Latin Core Vocabulary
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 204, 278, 319, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
Gellius from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-gellius).

phrases.latin: locum ante jānuam domūs vacuum, per quem ā viā aditus accessusque ad aedīs est
phrases.english: the empty space in front of the door of a house, through which one comes in from the street
